newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cambodia still eager to join ASEAN, premier says.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia still eager to join ASEAN, premier says.

text.p: Cambodia is still eager to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) despite strong reservations expressed by King Norodom Sihanouk, the king's son was quoted on Tuesday as saying.
The Singapore Straits Times newspaper quoted First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh as saying ASEAN membership would help Cambodia integrate its economy with its booming neighbours.
"My father continues to think of ASEAN as a political, military alliance like NATO and, therefore, it would be against the idea of neutrality," Ranariddh said an interview in Phnom Penh.
"But my approach is an economic approach. We view the move towards ASEAN as economic integration and Cambodia would benefit in terms of economic integration and development."
Last week King Sihanouk said he strongly opposed Cambodia joining the seven-member ASEAN because he feared disastrous economic and social costs.
Cambodia has observer status in the regional bloc but hopes to become a member in July alongside Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
ASEAN has said Cambodia, Laos and Burma would join simultaneously.
Sihanouk said he shared the views expressed recently in a memorandum attached to a palace release.
The memorandum, whose author was not named, said ASEAN membership would entail significant expenses, wipe out duty revenues of about $250 million and flood the country with imports.
